items.title: W.T. "Ed" Kirkeby Interview, 1961-06-28
items.q: and, of course, Adrian Rilline, who developed into the greatest bass saxophone player in the world. So we had a real team at that time

ctx.x: 1140 Broadway. In fact, I auditioned the original California Ramblers down at 1140 Broadway in the Paramount. And, of course, I made records for them under Ananda Plume by the original Ramblers, with Red Nichols and Jimmy Dorsey and Tommy Dorsey, and, of course, Adrian Rilline, who developed into the greatest bass saxophone player in the world. So we had a real team at that time, you know, with great stars. And, as I say, I think I used about 20 nom de plumes or more. And I think that, as far as recording is…
Well, I think more than any other man also, you've confused the picture for the jazz historian who tries to follow all the places you've been.
